architecture: Two agencies. National Rail: hub lock Liverpool Lime Street (LIV, seven TOCs), secondary hub Liverpool South Parkway (LPY, airport connector) — reuses the Thames Valley/Solent/West of England/Greater Manchester hub+secondary-hub pattern. Merseyrail: interchange pair Liverpool Central and Moorfields (both Merseyrail dual-line interchanges, no ranking given between them by the report), schedule-only v1 (no confirmed real-time feed). Liverpool Lime Street's Merseyrail presence is built as a SEPARATE stationGroup, doNotGroup: true against the National Rail Lime Street stationGroup, because the oracle report contradicts itself on whether the two agencies share platforms ('platform level', report line 41) or are separate buildings connected by footbridge ('separate infrastructure, separate entrance/footbridge', report line 73, C2/C3 point 2) — this pack takes the more conservative separate-infrastructure reading pending confirmation; see hazard-pack.md H1 and direction-model-memo.md.
agency: National Rail (Darwin/OpenLDBWS) — Northern Trains (primary franchise), Avanti West Coast, TransPennine Express, East Midlands Railway, Transport for Wales, West Midlands Trains, CrossCountry
Merseyrail (Serco / Transport UK Group concession) — Northern Line (39 stations) and Wirral Line (34 stations), 69 stations total, schedule-only v1

V1 SCOPE: this pack catalogs Merseyrail alongside National Rail, departing from the oracle report's own literal recommendation to defer Merseyrail to H2. CORRECTED 2 Sep 2026 at flip time: Merseyrail's static GTFS is confirmed live via Transitland, but no board of any kind was ever implemented — fetchMerseyrailStopBoard() throws MerseyrailFeedUnconfirmedError unconditionally, the same shape as Greater Manchester's Metrolink and South Yorkshire's Supertram. The original 'schedule-only, verdict in' framing didn't match that reality; Merseyrail's board-eligibility verdict is out-product, matching how those two sibling regions' own unconfirmed-feed layers are verdicted. See direction-model-memo.md for the original reasoning and the oracle report's Board eligibility section for the correction.

ARCHITECTURE: National Rail hub+secondary-hub pair (Lime Street / South Parkway) is structurally separate from Merseyrail's own interchange pair (Central / Moorfields). Liverpool Lime Street's Merseyrail presence is built as its own stationGroup, doNotGroup: true against the NR Lime Street stationGroup, because the report contradicts itself on whether the two share a building or are footbridge-connected separate buildings. See hazard-pack.md H1 — UNRESOLVED, flagged for Tim.

National Rail modes v1: heavy rail, destination-board model (not line+terminus). BLOCKED pending DARWIN_LDB_TOKEN — see coverageGaps. Build the catalog/adapter normally per Nico's report; do not wire the token until it exists.

Merseyrail modes v1: metro-style commuter rail, line+terminus model, SCHEDULE-ONLY (no confirmed real-time feed anywhere). This is a genuine feed-status gap, same kind as Greater Manchester's Metrolink gap and South Yorkshire's Supertram/SYFTL gap, not the standard National Rail account block. Do not conflate the two in downstream QA notes.

Hub lock (National Rail): Liverpool Lime Street (LIV CRS), National Rail terminus, seven TOCs (Northern Trains primary franchise; Avanti West Coast, TransPennine Express, East Midlands Railway, Transport for Wales, West Midlands Trains, CrossCountry through-running). Secondary hub (National Rail): Liverpool South Parkway (LPY CRS), airport connector (Liverpool John Lennon Airport), regional and long-distance services.

Interchange pair (Merseyrail): Liverpool Central and Moorfields, both 'dual-line interchange' per the report with no ranking given between them (contrast Greater Manchester's Metrolink report, which explicitly ranked St Peter's Square over Victoria). Neither built as sole hub lock over the other. Flagged for Tim/Nico if a real ranking exists.

doNotGroup: Liverpool Lime Street National Rail platforms vs Merseyrail interchange presence — relationship AMBIGUOUS in the source report (line 41 'platform level' vs line 73 / C2/C3 point 2 'separate infrastructure, separate entrance/footbridge', no distance/time figure given either way, unlike Manchester Victoria's or Manchester Piccadilly/Piccadilly Gardens' explicit figures). Built conservatively as two separate stationGroups. See hazard-pack.md H1 — NOT RESOLVED, open item for Tim.

Ellesmere Port (ELP CRS, Merseyrail Wirral Line terminus): tracker says this should fold into Liverpool City Region, not remain a separate picker city. `uk-ellesmere-port` currently exists as a STANDALONE registry entry (status 'planned') in lib/providers/registry.js. This pack's Merseyrail scope already includes Ellesmere Port as a Wirral Line terminus. NOT RESOLVED HERE — registry-scope decision is explicitly Jim/Tim's call, outside Luke's scope. Second flag of this issue (Nico flagged it first in research). See jim-handoff.md.
